result.result:
The gate returned **OK** on the first run (7 witnesses, 10 names, nothing composed), so I stopped there with 5 of the 6 runs unused.

**The rule** (`library/TrafficSpec/Rules/NRS_484B/NRS_484B_223_4b.lean`):
- **Class:** `x` is a member of the vehicle aggregate `DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle`.
- **Applicability:** `x` occupies a highway that has a single right turn lane. That means a turn lane on that highway whose side is right, which is the rightmost lane in its direction (ordinal equals count), and whose left neighbour is not also a right turn lane.
- **Obligation:** it repeats that whole lane selection, then forbids the car from leaving straight through an intersection that lane runs into. The check runs once, when the car leaves the intersection (rising edge of `drv_motion_straight_through_region`).
- **"While being driven in the right turn lane":** the car's footprint overlapped that lane at some observation between its latest entry into the intersection and its exit. The look-back stops at that entry, which is the onset the record declares.
- I made no narrowing of my own. The only open choice was putting the highway quantifier outside the lane quantifier, which matches the order in the record.

**The witnesses** (`library/TrafficSpecWitness/NRS_484B/NRS_484B_223_4b.lean`) sample every 50 ms, which is the reading's step bound. A car occupies every region its footprint overlaps, so at the moment it enters the intersection it is in both the lane and the intersection.

| Witness | Scene | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| forbid | Straight out of the single right turn lane | violated |
| blind | Same as forbid, with yaw rate masked | unknown |
| permit | 90° right turn inside the intersection | compliant |
| idle | No turn lane | not applicable |
| branch_1 | Straight from the through lane | compliant |
| branch_2 (added) | Two right turn lanes side by side, straight from the rightmost | not applicable |
| branch_3 (added) | As branch_2, plus a single right turn lane on the westbound approach that the car never uses | compliant |

I added branch_2 and branch_3 so the gate's adequacy check sees the "left neighbour is not a right turn lane" test do work. It appears twice, once in the applicability and once in the obligation, and each copy needs a witness that changes verdict without it.

Every witness is judged from 100 ms onward. At the first observation there is no earlier one to compare against, so the exit/entry checks there are undefined.

When I tried to check a file length, a shell command other than the gate was refused, as the task's rules require. Nothing depended on it.

`task_result.md` is in the working directory and records the gate run, the choices above and why I finished.
